title: Secretary of State of North Dakota

context.text: Both candidates were unopposed in their June 9, 2026 primaries (Howe 99.6%, Braunberger 99.8%, write-ins excepted).
Republicans hold a supermajority in the Legislature and all statewide elected offices, per the North Dakota Monitor.
The North Dakota Secretary of State's certified 2026 General Election candidate list shows two candidates for Secretary of State: Michael Howe and Ryan Braunberger.

candidates.name: Michael Howe
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 9, 2026 Republican primary with no declared opponent.

summary.text: Michael Howe is the Republican incumbent Secretary of State, a former state legislator first elected in 2022. In a July 2026 interview he said North Dakota's elections are secure, pointing to proof-of-citizenship checks at ID issuance, paper ballots and encrypted result reporting.

background.text: Former state lawmaker; elected Secretary of State in 2022.

priorities.text: Maintaining secure, auditable paper-ballot elections; says the voter file is updated daily with deaths and has not been shared with the Department of Homeland Security.

statements.context: Told the North Dakota Monitor that new North Dakota ID applicants must prove citizenship and that a North Dakota ID is needed to vote

candidates.name: Ryan Braunberger
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Democratic-NPL nomination; endorsed at the March 7 state convention.

summary.text: Ryan Braunberger is the Democratic-NPL nominee for Secretary of State and a Fargo state senator. He says he is running to boost public trust in elections; in July 2026 he agreed with Howe that North Dakota's voter data and results are secure.

background.text: Born in Fargo; earned a bachelor's degree in social work from Minnesota State University Moorhead in 2022 and an associate degree in business administration in 2007.
Fargo state senator (District 10), first elected in 2022.

priorities.text: Boost public trust in elections and civic engagement; continue to protect North Dakotans' voter data privacy.
More educational outreach on the 2025 law requiring mail ballots to be in election officials' hands by the time polls close.

statements.quote: Obviously, we ask at the polling stations, ‘Are you 18? Are you a North Dakota resident? And, are you a U.S. citizen?’
statements.context: North Dakota Monitor interview, describing polling-place eligibility checks
